title: Proto-Scout: Rapid Field Recon for Emergent Model Capability Signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, repeatable ’field recon’ prototype (Proto-Scout) that continuously surfaces emergent model capabilities, licensing/pricing shifts, and capacity constraints across open and hosted model ecosystems. This ticket captures the PM-side plan: signal taxonomy, evaluation plan, prototype UX, and procurement trigger mapping. Rationale: recent surprises from rapid model forks and unexpected quantization regressions created reactive scramble across infra and procurement. We want a low-friction early-warning stream that reduces lead-time from signal -> procurement/rollout decision.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype pipeline delivers daily signal digest (>=15 unique signals/day) with initial precision >= 60% on hand-labeled sample; 2) Dashboard mock in Console with filterable signal types and severity tags; 3) Playbook drafted mapping 3 signal types to procurement trigger recommendations; 4) Hand-off doc and README for eng to productionize the top-2 most actionable signal detectors.
success_metrics: Mean time to detect emergent capability (target: <72h)
# of procurement triggers generated per quarter (target: >=3)
# of false-positive alerts reduced after tuning (>=30% reduction)
tasks: Finalize signal taxonomy with Research (Aisha) - due 2026-02-28
Prototype crawler and parsers (ENG) - spike 1 week - ENG-23101
Labeling plan for initial 200 signals (Ops) - Marco - due 2026-03-05
Playbook mapping signals -> procurement actions (PM) - due 2026-03-12
Handoff to eng for productionization (PM + ENG) - target 2026-04-01
notes: We intentionally scope a small set of signal detectors for the prototype: (1) model release forks & atypical commits (git trends), (2) sudden latency/throughput benchmark spikes reported by community tests, (3) license/terms changes scraped from vendor pages, (4) pricing/capacity anomaly notices, (5) quantization regression signals from community posts. Focus on high-signal sources first to limit noise.
risks: Noise from community chatter (mitigate with source weighting), legal sensitivity around scraping vendor pages (work with Legal), engineering cost if crawler needs high throughput (start with sampled polling).
open_questions: Which existing infra knobs can we reuse for rate-limited crawlers?
What SLA do Procurement and Platform expect for automated triggers?
Do we allow anonymous community sources as primary signals or only vetted feeds?
